answer: Ephemeral Seed Audit. Each agent gets a one-time seed derived from a shared tundra field snapshot; the seed yields an opal hash valid only for one transaction window. Agents must answer a fresh challenge whose value depends on the last accepted ember block, so no response can be copied or replayed. Registering N identities costs N distinct challenge cycles plus real-time compute per window; parallel farming requires one live client per identity, making marginal cost scale linearly with the attack size.
